title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes concern the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. A = k{T} is read here as the divided-power polynomial algebra Γ_k(T), with basis T^{[n]}; this reading is an inference from the context, since the page does not define it. Locally at p one uses the generators T_s = T^{[p^s]}. They satisfy T_s^p = p·ν_s·T_{s+1}, where ν_s = (p^{s+1})!/(p·(p^s!)^p) is a p-adic unit. The ν'_s on the page are such units.

Computation (top half). Grothendieck is analysing a homogeneous module map u of degree −d from a truncation τ_α(M ⊗ Γ) (degrees ≥ α) to N ⊗ Γ. He writes the relevant component of u as a product of a coefficient and a monomial in the T_i:
- η_s = ξ_s · T_ν^{δ_ν} ⋯ T_{r−1}^{δ_{r−1}} · (T_{r−1} ⋯ T_{s−1})^{p−1}, with ξ_s ∈ M.
- Multiplying by T_s^{p−1} raises the last product to (T_r ⋯ T_s)^{p−1}.
- The A-linearity relation (R_s), η_s T_s^{p−1} = p ν'_s η_{s+1}, then gives, after comparing coefficients of the same monomial, ξ_s = p ν'_s ξ_{s+1}.
- Iterating: ξ_s = p^k ν'_s ⋯ ν'_{s+k−1} ξ_{s+k} for every k ≥ 1.
- Hence ξ_s ∈ ∩_k p^k M. That is, the coefficients are infinitely p-divisible and lie in the divisible part.

Integral sanity check. Write u(T^{[n]}) = c_n T^{[n−d]}. Since T·T^{[n]} = (n+1) T^{[n+1]}, linearity gives (n+1) c_{n+1} = (n−d+1) c_n. So c_α must be divisible by ever larger integers.

Proposition. Let k be a commutative ring, A = k{T}, and M, N two k-modules (flatness is added tentatively, with a question mark). Let N_0 = ∩_{n ≥ 1} nN be the divisible submodule, and α ≥ d. Then every u ∈ Hom^{−d}(τ_α M_{S_k}, N_{S_k}) factors through N_{0,S_k}. A marginal note says this Hom module is independent of α, up to restriction. Equivalently, Hom^{−d}(τ_α M, N_0) → Hom^{−d}(τ_α M, N) is an isomorphism.

Corollary. If N_0 = 0 (for example k torsion, i.e. killed by some n), then these negative-degree Homs vanish.

Purpose. This is a rigidity/vanishing lemma: there are no nontrivial degree-lowering PD-module maps (equivalently, maps between Tate-twisted or shifted PD objects). It is presumably used to show that some negative Hom or Ext groups in the PD de Rham setting vanish, or are controlled by divisible parts.
errors: The computation is only sketched. The exponent bookkeeping (T_{r−1} in η_s versus T_r after multiplying by T_s^{p−1}) looks inconsistent as transcribed, possibly a slip for T_r ⋯ T_{s−1}.

The page only treats the p-primary part. Passing from ∩_k p^k M for each p to ∩_n nN needs all primes, plus flatness or torsion-freeness to compare coefficients. This is presumably why 'plats' was added with a question mark.

The page first concludes divisibility for the source coefficients ξ_s ∈ M, but the proposition states factorisation through the divisible part of the target N. The roles are not fully reconciled on the page.

ideas.what: In divided-power algebras, (T^{[p^s]})^p = p·unit·T^{[p^{s+1}]}, which forces infinite p-divisibility of coefficients of degree-lowering linear maps
ideas.modern_name: Structure of the PD polynomial algebra Γ(T); vanishing of negative-degree Hom between PD-modules

ideas.what: Negative-degree Homs from truncated M⊗Γ(T) to N⊗Γ(T) factor through the divisible part of N, and vanish when k is torsion
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity/vanishing lemma for graded PD-modules (cf. Hom out of the PD affine line G_a^#)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; folklore in crystalline / PD de Rham theory

deep.surprise_reason: A routine technical lemma about divided-power polynomial modules (negative-degree maps are infinitely divisible). It is correct in spirit and of the kind any specialist would derive; nothing suggests an unrecorded result.
transcription_corrections: '$p\nu'_s \xi_{s+1}$' on the right of the third display appears as '$p\nu'_s$' with a superscript-like mark; the meaning (relation R_s) is unchanged.
'$\xi_s \in [-p-] \bigcap_k (p^k M)$': the struck-out symbol is a crossed-out p; read ξ_s ∈ ∩_k p^k M.
'{+ plats [?]+}' is uncertain; it may read 'plus grand' or similar. The insertion over N_0 reads 'sous-module divisible'.
